issue.title: The scratch page draws a stock glTF export of one loc and the 16 square
issue.body:
## Parent

#82

## Spec

`spec/82-gltf-export-findings.md` (Method; Findings table, rows 2 and 3; Success criteria 3)

## What to build

Start the note `docs/research/82-gltf-export.md` and the scratch setup that every later task reuses. Nothing in scratch is committed. The scratch folder is `~/tmp/2026-11-15-82-gltf-export`, and the note calls it `<scratch folder>`.

- **Scratch page.** A bare three.js page with a local copy of the latest stable three.js and its glTF and Draco loaders, with no CDN. `?t=<seconds>` freezes the clip at that time and `?view=<name>` selects a camera. It draws no shadow, and it reports `renderer.info.render.calls` and the frame rate.
- **Screenshots.** A headless browser on the real GPU (Playwright with Chrome, or the same in another tool) takes the page screenshots. Record the WebGL renderer string. Stop and report if it is a software renderer.
- **Stock export.** Import region `48_50` of snapshot 430. Export one loc with a textured face first, then the terrain of the 16 square centred on about tile 3080, 3250, both with Blender's stock glTF exporter. Read the glTF JSON after each export.
- **Row 2.** Read the sampler of a texture that has Closest interpolation.
- **Row 3.** Read how the terrain's Emission material exports, load it on the page, and compare a screenshot with an unlit Blender render at the same camera. Read both pictures.
- **Environment.** The note names the Blender version, every exporter setting that is not the default, the three.js release, the machine's GPU and the browser. It records the scratch commands with placeholders for local paths.
- The note has the findings table with all 14 rows and the size table, with the rows of later tasks left empty.

The commit holds the note and the spec file, which is not committed yet.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/research/82-gltf-export.md` has rows 2 and 3 filled: survives or not, the glTF JSON extract or the pair of pictures in words, and each cause marked as evidence or as a guess.
- [ ] The note names the Blender version, the exporter settings that are not the default, the three.js release, the GPU and the browser, and gives the commands to repeat the export and the screenshot.
- [ ] `<scratch folder>` has a page that takes `?t=` and `?view=`, loads three.js from a local copy and reports draw calls and frame rate.
- [ ] The commit holds only the note and the spec, and `prek run --all-files` passes.

## Verification

```bash
prek run --all-files
```

Manual: the commands in the note reproduce the two exports and the row 3 screenshot.

parent.title: Export a region and a player with a clip to glTF
parent.body:
As an engineer, I want to export a region and a player with a clip from Blender to glTF, so that a three.js page shows them with the same look as the Blender viewport.

The first use is the 3D scene on my profile page: region `48_50` from #35 with my player standing in it on an idle clip. The spec of #35 left the glTF export for a later issue, and this is that issue.

Right now nothing in the add-on has been exported to glTF, so I don't know what survives Blender's exporter. I think most of the work is finding that out first, and then fixing what doesn't survive.

Not settled yet:

- Whether the face colours, face alpha and textures of a model survive the export, and what three.js material they end up as.
- How render priority gets to the page. glTF has no field for it, so stacked faces probably need something else (e.g. a small offset or a draw order on the three.js side).
- How the scenery materials export. The terrain material is unlit, but the scenery materials use Principled BSDF, so the two would be lit differently on the page. The page wants the flat 2007 look with no shadows first.
- Whether a Bones-method clip plays in three.js. The first check is idle plus one emote.
- Whether a clip that changes face alpha can export at all, or whether the first version only takes clips that don't.
- Whether the export writes shared mesh data once. `48_50` has 185 shared meshes, and the spec of #35 left this question for the export issue.
- How big the result is. `48_50` is 4096 tiles and 1894 objects, and the page has to stay light, so it probably needs a smaller rectangle of tiles or joined meshes.
- Whether this is an operator in the add-on, a script that calls Blender's exporter, or only a doc with the export settings.
